title: The Bicycle Powered by Applause
premise: A kinetic team needs the audience to clap in an exact impossible rhythm.
pressure: A kinetic bicycle sculpture runs only when spectators clap in a rhythm nobody can sustain. Its riders are spent and the marshal has little daylight left for the road course. A sponsor wants them to try again for the camera.
investigate: Time the wheel motion against safe clapping intervals and inspect the drive chain
success: The applause controls a slipping clutch, not magic horsepower. The crew records the flaw and can repair it without another public exhaustion test.
failure: The rhythm breaks under the crowd's enthusiasm. A rider spots the worn linkage while you slow the restart.
help: Help the team choose a safe withdrawal or rest break without public shaming
helpOutcome: The riders drink water and accept a tow to the next repair area. The crowd claps for the decision rather than demanding another lap.

title: Glorious Competitor Number Minus One
premise: An unregistered sculpture was in every historic starting photo.
pressure: A sculpture numbered minus one appears in race photographs taken years before its maker was born. Officials want to erase the pictures to fix the record. The volunteer archivist would rather label what nobody understands.
investigate: Compare negatives, registration books and paint details without adding a convenient inventor
success: Across three decades the same tiny repair crew stands behind the vehicle. Their faces are indistinct; their tools and homemade badge are not.
failure: The copied registration numbers run together in the scanner. A retired mechanic still recognizes the paint, and asks you to preserve the original print.
help: Invite the maker and retired volunteers to describe only what they actually know
helpOutcome: The competitor gets a place to start, not a fabricated biography. The archive adds a small card reading ORIGIN UNVERIFIED.

title: The Engineering Judge from Elsewhere
premise: A judge gives perfect scores for violating Earth's physics.
pressure: A judge gives perfect marks to sculptures that ignore gravity. The ordinary builders object because their wheels, unlike everyone else's, must still touch the road. The judge insists the rubric is clear and refuses to show it.
investigate: Ask for one measurable criterion and insist it applies to every entrant
success: The scoring sheet predicts a loose wheel at the bay crossing. The crew checks the axle first; the judge gives them no points for avoiding disaster.
failure: The judge's demonstration leaves neither tracks nor witnesses. You record the failed test instead of awarding it the benefit of a supernatural doubt.
help: Help the competitors draft fair judging rules that can survive an absurd race
helpOutcome: The organizers publish rules rewarding practical ingenuity and crew safety. The impossible vehicles remain welcome, but no longer exempt from explaining themselves.

title: The Racer Who Is a Whole Committee
premise: Six people insist they are one entrant, and somehow all are correct.
pressure: Six kinetic racers insist they are one contestant. Their vehicle moves only when all six disagree on which lever to pull, a design decision the registration clerk cannot fit into the form's box marked CAPTAIN. None of the crew wants to surrender their vote to make paperwork happy.
investigate: Inspect the linkage while all six demonstrate how they share control
success: The mechanism passes force through a gap you can measure but cannot cross. Beneath the frame sits an older race number; the six disagree about whether to paint over it, and leave it visible.
failure: The chain splits during the test. All six describe the same movement from different seats, giving the mechanic enough information to isolate the fault.
help: Ask officials to register the crew as a team without making one person their owner
helpOutcome: The clerk accepts six names and one machine. The crew draws lots for starting order and keeps its argument, which seems to be part of the propulsion system.

title: The Noon Siren at Midnight
premise: The race launches at noon, midnight and both at once.
pressure: The starting siren sounds both at noon and midnight; two crowds occupy Arcata Plaza without seeing each other. A volunteer marshal is trying to keep a children's group out of a launch lane that seems to exist twice.
investigate: Compare recording timestamps from the two starting lines while staying clear of the race
success: The same whistle has two timestamps and a harbor echo. The marshal keeps the recordings while treating the live course as the only one crews should enter.
failure: Your phone clips the noise into static, but the second crowd's cheer remains on another volunteer's recording.
help: Help the marshal separate the visible racers and route spectators to safe viewing space
helpOutcome: The actual teams launch after a fresh headcount. The midnight crowd applauds on a delay, which is almost courteous.

title: Deadman's Drop, Then Up Again
premise: A kinetic sculpture rolls downhill so vigorously it reaches yesterday.
pressure: A kinetic sculpture hits Dead Man's Drop and reaches yesterday with sand still caught in its goggles. Its exhausted crew wants to attempt the descent again to prove the story, although a brake cable has begun to fray.
investigate: Compare the crew's route log and the mechanical wear before considering another descent
success: The sand sample and log disagree about time but agree the brake is failing. The crew retires the run and preserves both clues.
failure: The date on the log smears in a wet glove. A volunteer spots the frayed cable and marks the vehicle unfit before anyone repeats the drop.
help: Help the crew secure the sculpture and arrange recovery from the course
helpOutcome: Everyone reaches the repair point unhurt. The sculpture's clock insists it has already received tomorrow's safety inspection.

title: Sand Castle with a Mayor
premise: A miniature government attempts to reroute the race.
pressure: A sandcastle has elected a mayor and declared the dune an independent municipality. Its first ordinance is a seashell toll on the kinetic race. The crew wants the shortest route, while a volunteer points out that the castle's disputed territory includes fragile dune plants.
investigate: Ask the tiny mayor for a boundary map and compare it with the marked habitat zone
success: The castle survey shows a real patch of sensitive vegetation that the current course tape misses. The volunteer corrects the tape and the mayor requests credit in the minutes.
failure: A wave erases city hall and most of the border posts. Its surviving bylaw is legible enough to show the habitat boundary still matters.
help: Help the racers plot a detour that protects the plants without humiliating a sand government
helpOutcome: The racers wheel around the protected area. The sandcastle stamps a seashell permit, which immediately disintegrates in a pocket but counts as diplomacy.

title: The Dune that Swallowed the Map
premise: A traveling dune relocates three of the player's remembered destinations.
pressure: A dune swallows the kinetic course map and three destinations appear to migrate across the page. A mechanic sees her team's finish line somewhere beyond the protected grass and wants to follow it before the marshal can object.
investigate: Compare the moving map with current flagged route markers and the tide plan
success: The map's shifting edge points to a lost survey peg, but the legal route is unchanged. The mechanic marks both on a separate sketch.
failure: The paper tears and takes the supposed shortcut with it. A sand-streaked photograph still shows the official markers intact.
help: Help the team follow the safe course without crossing habitat closures
helpOutcome: The racers take the marked detour and reach the water stage. The dune keeps the map; the volunteer keeps the dune grass out of trouble.

title: The Bribe That Bribes Itself
premise: A customary race bribe becomes sentient and offers a better deal.
pressure: A traditional race bribe has developed a voice and promises to reverse tomorrow's disputed judging in exchange for cheers. A young team built its sculpture from donated wheels and cannot afford a protest fee, let alone a sentient favor.
investigate: Check the stated judging rules and ask how the bribe claims to change them
success: The bribe quotes a rule that was never adopted. You bring the real scoring sheet to the teams before rumor becomes an official result.
failure: The object vanishes when the chair arrives. Its promises survive in three accounts that contradict one another; the actual scores can still be checked.
help: Help the young team file a fair objection without buying an advantage
helpOutcome: A volunteer finds the appeal form and waives no rule for anyone. The bribe sulks in a costume pocket, outbid by transparent paperwork.

title: The Official Unofficial Rescue Team
premise: A crew of cryptids performs cheerful and competent roadside repairs.
pressure: A cryptid rescue crew is replacing a broken axle in the dunes with ordinary tools and several impossible hands. A sponsor wants exclusive rights to their faces and calls it the price of receiving help.
investigate: Document the mechanical repair rather than the rescuers' identities
success: The replacement axle carries the unknown racer's maker's mark. The team records it for inspection, without photographing a volunteer who has asked for privacy.
failure: The lead mechanic slips away before you can ask about the mark. The repair remains safe and its tool scratches give the crew a trace to compare later.
help: Help the crew protect the rescuers' consent and feed everyone doing the repair
helpOutcome: The sculpture moves again. The rescue crew accepts sandwiches and no publicity; the sponsor learns that gratitude is not a media release.

title: A Floating Sculpture with Opinions
premise: The craft refuses to float until its design philosophy is heard.
pressure: A floating sculpture refuses to launch until its makers admit that a boat can also be art and still be expected to float. The artist calls this censorship; the skipper calls it a buoyancy problem; the spectators have started betting on which one gets wet first.
investigate: Test the flotation chambers and let the sculpture explain what it is refusing
success: A sealed compartment contains a chart of a second channel beneath the bay, dated after this race. The skipper photographs the chart before anyone claims it proves a safe crossing.
failure: Your test soaks a row of spectators, and the boat declines to move. The crew apologizes, closes the launch lane and finds the missing ballast entry.
help: Help the crew redesign the hull without treating their artwork as a joke
helpOutcome: The team adds flotation and a sensible launch plan while preserving the outrageous silhouette. It enters the water as art, not a wager on the rescue crew.

title: The Second Water Crossing
premise: A mirror bay exists briefly just beneath the first.
pressure: A mirror crossing opens briefly beneath the real bay, showing one team an empty channel and another the racers who disappeared yesterday. Both crews want to launch first. The safety boat is already committed to the actual course.
investigate: Compare the mirror's landmarks with today's marked water route from shore
success: A reflection matches an old channel survey rather than a safe route. You record it and leave navigation to the marshals.
failure: The mirror folds away before anyone agrees on the bearings. A safety volunteer has drawn the vanished marker position in a waterproof notebook.
help: Keep both crews off the unmarked crossing until rescue coverage is available
helpOutcome: The teams queue for the authorized launch and neither vanishes. One sculpture's reflection keeps paddling for a second after its crew stops.

title: The Cosmic Coast Guard
premise: A rescue boat has paperwork from a galaxy that no longer exists.
pressure: A rescue boat approaches the kinetic water crossing under a coast-guard flag from a galaxy absent from every map. The uniformed crew demand impossible forms before helping a stalled racer. Actual local rescuers are already working, and the tide is not accepting paperwork.
investigate: Compare the strange vessel's rescue log with the local dispatch record
success: The log lists a boat whose name has not yet appeared on the race register. The dispatch volunteer writes down the discrepancy, then sends everyone back to the immediate rescue.
failure: The crew salute and depart before identifying their authority. Their wake travels against the current; a local skipper witnessed it and stays with the stranded racers.
help: Coordinate with local rescue volunteers before offering the unknown crew a role
helpOutcome: The sailors quietly take a line when invited and follow the local rescue lead. The racer reaches shore without signing away anybody's judgment.

title: The Tide Swaps Places with Time
premise: The protagonist can save equipment or rescue a stranger's memory.
pressure: For one minute the tide and time exchange jobs. A stranger asks you to save a memory of her brother while a crew's electrical gear is sliding off the dock. You can act on one danger immediately; the other needs a witness who will listen.
investigate: Identify what the stranger can verify and where the equipment will land
success: You learn the memory is tied to a photo still safely ashore. The crew recovers the gear before it reaches open water.
failure: The minute snaps shut before you can reconstruct either timeline. A case slips beneath the dock; the stranger cannot say whether her brother's photograph was taken here or somewhere else. You mark the current for the crew and write down her description without completing it for her. Both losses remain losses.
help: Call for a second helper and keep the stranger out of the water
helpOutcome: The crew saves the equipment and the stranger reaches her friend, who remembers the same photograph. Nobody has to choose between grief and a life jacket.

title: The Race Officials' Secret Ballot
premise: Judges quietly decide which version of the county survives.
pressure: Race officials reveal six ballots for six possible futures of the county. In each version, a different crew's work has been erased from the record. One judge wants the players to choose immediately, before affected racers can see what their votes would hide.
investigate: Compare each ballot with the deeds and people actually recorded during the race
success: The tally includes acts of repair, kindness and risk witnessed on the course. None of the six futures tells the whole story, and the clerk agrees to preserve the original evidence.
failure: The sealed ballot box vanishes between counting tables. A marshal retains the sign-in sheet and insists the unrepresented crews be heard before another vote.
help: Demand a public account of what each proposal costs before anyone decides
helpOutcome: The officials post the alternatives and invite the affected teams to speak. A ballot cannot fairly settle a county's future if half its people were never allowed in the room.

title: The Trophy with a Pulse
premise: A trophy congratulates winners and whispers the county's original name.
pressure: The winner's trophy beats like a small heart and whispers a county name nobody recognizes. The crew is afraid accepting it will erase the hours they built together. The announcer is waiting for a photograph; the makers want a moment without spectators.
investigate: Check the inscription against the event ledger and ask the crew what they want recorded
success: The trophy's plaque bears an impossible alternate date. The official ledger preserves the crew's actual result no matter what the object calls the county.
failure: The name fades when you copy it. A teammate still has a photo of the plaque and everyone remembers who built the machine.
help: Give the crew space to decide whether to accept the prize together
helpOutcome: They take a team photo holding their own battered tool box. The trophy waits on its plinth, briefly the least important thing onstage.

title: The Finish Line Moves
premise: A finish banner vanishes whenever someone claims to have solved the mystery.
pressure: The finish banner in Ferndale slides another block away every time a competitor announces that the county's mystery is solved. The exhausted racers keep running toward it, and a child with a homemade medal has been standing in the cold at the supposed finish.
investigate: Test whether the banner responds to a question instead of another grand claim
success: The banner settles beside an old road sign long enough for the race marshal to record its position. It moves again when somebody shouts the answer, which proves remarkably little.
failure: Your test sends the banner retreating past the next corner. You at least learn which announcement triggered the move, and stop using it as the finish line.
help: Put up an ordinary safe finish that every tired team can actually reach
helpOutcome: A volunteer stretches a ribbon between two chairs. Every team crosses it, receives water and gets counted, whether or not anyone has decoded the moving banner.

title: The Ghost of Hobart's Contraption
premise: A legendary mechanical inspiration requests one final impossible modification.
pressure: A ghostly engineer offers the kinetic crew one last modification: a lever that would make the sculpture sail beautifully and become impossible to steer. The exhausted fabricator is tempted to prove the design could work.
investigate: Sketch the proposed mechanism and compare it with the crew's tested controls
success: The elegant lever would bypass a safety stop. The fabricator keeps the drawing as art and leaves the real steering intact.
failure: The engineer disappears before explaining the linkage. The crew saves a rough sketch and rejects an untested change at the finish line.
help: Help the fabricator credit the idea without risking the riders
helpOutcome: They paint the ghost's initials on a spare panel and finish with the tested rig. The engineer applauds the restraint, the most unlikely part of the haunting.

title: Every Version of the Winner
premise: Five parallel champions arrive, all insisting they already met the player.
pressure: Five champions arrive at the finish wearing five different medals. Each remembers you doing something different. One credits you for a rescue you never made; the actual volunteer who performed it is standing ten feet away, unnoticed.
investigate: Compare the five stories with the race log and named witnesses
success: Three accounts share a true timing error, but none agrees on the winner. The marshal preserves the evidence and records the real volunteer's role.
failure: The champions wander into the crowd before you identify the shared mistake. You still collect two names and the volunteer's original incident report.
help: Make room for the rescuer to tell their own story before anyone hands out medals
helpOutcome: The volunteer gets thanked, the ceremony continues, and the five champions decide to share a podium built for two.

title: The County Finally Votes
premise: The player's relationships, evidence and choices determine the surviving ending.
pressure: The county ballot offers wilderness, industry, spectacle and shared stewardship in four tidy boxes. A clerk says your deeds count more than your speech. Around you are people who will live with the result, including those no campaign bothered to invite.
investigate: Compare the ballot summary with the actual decisions and the people affected
success: The campaign slogans cannot contain the evidence you collected. The clerk adds your verified account to the record, without promising which future wins.
failure: A projector fails before you can display the last document. You still name where the evidence can be found, and another witness offers to corroborate it.
help: Make room for someone affected by the proposal who has not been heard
helpOutcome: The meeting grows messier and more representative. No one agrees on a miracle. The county has to make its choice in public.
